subject: social
name: Social Studies
course: Early American Civilizations, European Exploration & the American Revolution
title: Grade 5 Social Studies: Early American Civilizations, European Exploration & the American Revolution
overview: Grade 5 Social Studies builds civic competence, geographical literacy, economic understanding, and historical inquiry aligned with the C3 Framework.
competencies: Investigate historical questions using multiple primary and secondary sources.
Analyze human and physical geography to understand how location and resources shape human decisions.
Explain economic concepts including production, market exchange, trade specialization, and public finance.
Apply democratic principles and civic virtues to deliberate contemporary public issues.

modules.title: Indigenous Civilizations of North America & European Exploration
modules.description: Studying diverse American Indian cultures (Pueblo, Haudenosaunee, Pacific Coast, Plains) and the impacts of transatlantic voyages.

topics.title: Complex Indigenous Societies of North America
topics.description: Analyzing governance, trade networks, architecture, and environmental adaptations before 1492.

topics.title: The Age of Exploration and the Columbian Exchange
topics.description: Investigating Spanish, French, and English explorations and global exchanges of crops and diseases.

modules.title: Thirteen British Colonies, Slavery & Economic Systems
modules.description: Contrasting New England, Middle, and Southern colonial regions, and examining the transatlantic slave trade.

topics.title: New England, Middle, and Southern Colonial Life
topics.description: Comparing religious dissent in Massachusetts, trade in Philadelphia, and plantation agriculture in Virginia.

topics.title: The Middle Passage and Enslaved Labor
topics.description: Examining the brutality of the transatlantic slave trade and the cultural resilience of enslaved Africans.

modules.title: The American Revolution & the United States Constitution
modules.description: Analyzing the causes of colonial revolt, the Declaration of Independence, the Revolutionary War, and constitutional democracy.

topics.title: Causes of the Revolution: Taxation Without Representation
topics.description: Exploring the Stamp Act, Boston Tea Party, Continental Congress, and Declaration of Independence.

topics.title: Creating the Constitution and the Bill of Rights
topics.description: Analyzing the Constitutional Convention, three branches of government, checks and balances, and rights.
